author: Astrokillah
text:
Honestly bro, I had one 'aha' moment lately, and that is, I started to
 pay attention to just 1 pair, USDJPY, and I only look at 1-min chart, I
 see how price was dancing around, how they created an FL, destroyed
another, created another, I see how price reacting to these FL, why some
 FL held price and some didn't.

Doing this allow me to learn quickly and not afraid to take trades. I
used to trade H4, because I was 'sold' by the believe that LTF candles
are messy, noisy, unreliable. But you know if you want to make 3R, 4R on
 H4/D1 timeframes, you have to wait a long long time. But if you follow 1
 min chart, you can get lots of 3R, 4R opportunities in a day.

I have a friend whom I considered being born in Mars. The guy is a
Master Scalper! He scalped on average 350 pips a day consistently, he
fired like 20-40 trades a day on M15, M5, M1 timeframes, and he would
happily take 10 pips profit on each trade. It's funny, because most of
the time, he posted a chart on whatsapp, telling me that he just got in a
 trade, within a few seconds, he sent another message again (I'm out,
all cleared!). And how did he do that? he basically trade kinks (he
called them flags), price move from flag to flag, he just trade small
bounces between these flags, he doesn't even wait for price to reach the
 opposing flag, he's very conservative, he closes his trade way before
price hit the opposing flag. His account this year (2017) is up like
600% and he trades off his cellphone, no PC needed!

author: Astrokillah
text:
LOL Ysbail, that's exactly how I am feeling now!

I think REALLY beginning to see the light! This ENGULF concept is
playing out marvelously.. over and over again... I now call it the
FIRST LAW OF ENGULF.

Remember this EURGBP trade I am still in? I was in at point 1, I closed
half position at point 2 so I can not lose on this trade. What did price
 do next?

It broke two LFL below point 2, and at point 3, 4, 5, 6, it came close
to touch the next orange FL. My friend told me, man.. why are you still
 in this trade? it can't break below, it's going to reverse and stop you
 out. But I have developed so much faith in RTM (is it a good thing?!
 ), I told him just wait and see. Because the FIRST LAW OF ENGULF says:
"Price has to hit the bottom orange FL before it can reverse up and
break above the top". So I see price dancing around, up and down,
messing around with people's mind. I must admit that if I really had
200% faith in RTM, I would have taken another short when price spike up
near my entry around point 5. But ok, I only have 95% faith. I keep my
cool, and I want to prove to myself that price WOULD indeed hit that
orange LFL.

And it did.... the FIRST LAW OF ENGULF, or maybe we should call it the FIRST LAW of RTM?!? And we need to patent it!

UPDATE: WOWOW ...just as I finished typing, price not only hit the
orange LFL, it broke through it and hit my TP! RTM made me speechless

author: Astrokillah
text:
Oh yes, bro, consistency is the most important thing, plus the
compounding effect. If you pay attention to your RR, I saw the equity
curve of the friend of mine who scalps a lot. He can double his account
easily. I asked him, why don't you let your account compound? If you
make 200% every year, you start with 50k, your account will compound to
200 million in 6 years!?! His answer was:" Son, my account is 200k, and I
 will withdraw my profit when it reach 400k and I will start again with
200k, I don't want to compound, I don't want my account to grow to 200
million because that will attract too much attention, my broker will not
 let me go easy, they do all their can to steal my money!"

He also pointed out that, do not dream that you can compound your
account from 50k to 200 million easily, because to do that you need to
trade with ever increasing lot size, and imagine, when you have spent
6-10 years buiding your account to 200 million, and then something like
Swiss Tsunami hit, that would wipe out your decades of hard work. So he
said, never dream of eternal compounding, we need to withdraw our
profit.

author: Astrokillah
text:
Analyzing Master's trades are key to our learning. I am re-reading
Master Salivan's journal and re-analyze each and everyone of his trade.
 Here's one that I need to stick on my wall. Very often when I took a
trade, let's say a long trade, I set my SL, and TP, and then I became
completely switched off. I could not put my mind into thinking about
trading in both direction. There are two different schools of thought:

- One says, you should set your TP at place where you want to take the opposite trade.

- The other one says, you should set your TP at conservative TG.

Which one is correct? well, I think they are both correct! For now, I
just need to learn how not to miss trade in the opposite direction once
my TP is hit.

Hi AK,

I don't think it was a bad trade, but to be honest, the real engulfs,
the ones that respect RTM latest strict rules and you have 99%
probability with, are just almost impossible to find, especially on LTF.
 Some days ago i went over my old trades of the year, and for the ones
that i tried to trade these engulfs on LTF, 90% were losses, probably
because they weren't real engulfs.

You might have seen latest IF's or Edge's posts, targets are everywhere
most of the time, so the real EG are really hard to find.

On HTF though i sometimes get to see them, it can help you to transform a
 little TT in Something big, that's how i try to use them now, after
months of failure into searching the 100% probability engulfs.

So my opinion is: if you see what you saw, that's odd enhancer, but
don't consider it 100% probability, because there is probably a line or
Something that come from the past and that you haven't seen
